title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
summary: Given an integer mountain array arr of length n with values increasing to a peak and then decreasing, find the index of the peak element.
statement: Given an integer mountain array arr of length n with values increasing to a peak and then decreasing, find the index of the peak element. Solve this in O(log(n)) time complexity.
constraints: arr strictly rises to one peak then strictly falls.
Return the peak index in logarithmic time.
reference_solution:
def mountain_peak_index(arr):
 left,right=0,len(arr)-1
 while left<right:
  middle=(left+right)//2
  if arr[middle]<arr[middle+1]:left=middle+1
  else:right=middle
 return left
hints: The slope at middle reveals which side contains the unique peak.
Binary-search with a closed candidate interval.
If arr[mid]<arr[mid+1], peak is right; otherwise peak is at mid or left.
Strict mountain shape guarantees the slope changes exactly once, so each comparison discards only nonpeak indices.
editorial: Strict mountain shape guarantees the slope changes exactly once, so each comparison discards only nonpeak indices.

tests.explanation: The maximum one is at index one.
The sequence changes from rising to falling at index one.
